title: Perfect complexes form a thick subcategory
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. In D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]: (1) if K\to L\to M\to K[1] is a distinguished triangle and two of K, L, M are perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], then so is the third; (2) if K\oplus L is perfect, then K and L are perfect; (3) shifts and finite direct sums of perfect objects are perfect.

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle, the two-out-of-three assertion is exactly Tag 08CR, applied to the three objects K, L, and M.
The direct-summand assertion is Tag 08CS, applied to the decomposition K ≅ L ⊕ M; it gives perfectness of each summand.

For each perfect object, choose an open cover on which it is represented by a strictly perfect complex, as in [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For finitely many objects, refine these covers to their common intersections. On each intersection, shifting a strictly perfect complex just reindexes its finitely many nonzero terms, and the termwise finite direct sum of finitely many strictly perfect complexes is again bounded with every term a direct summand of a finite free module. These local representatives therefore represent the shifted and finite-direct-sum objects, proving the closure assertion from Definition 08CM.
